description: Eval set for testing whether a candidate LLM is reliable enough to grade free-response Spanish exercises (translation, error-correction) across A1 and A2. Not built from Jodie's own tracked error history - she's still early in Spanish (finishing A2.2, 7 months in) and doesn't have that data yet. Instead, each category targets a well-documented, high-frequency mistake type for English-speaking learners of Spanish, drawn from the topics in spanish_grammar_catalogue.py (both the A1 and A2 books). Worth revisiting/replacing with a personal-error-pattern version later, the same way the German set was built, once real recurring mistakes become visible from actual usage.
spanish_variety: Peninsular Spanish, while accepting standard alternatives from other varieties unless the exercise explicitly targets a regional distinction.
how_to_use: For each item, send the 'sentence' and any optional 'grading_context' to the candidate model with the same prompt you plan to use in the real grading endpoint (e.g. 'Does this Spanish sentence correctly express the stated meaning? If not, identify the error and give the corrected form.').
Compare the model's verdict against 'is_correct' and, for incorrect items, its proposed fix against 'correct_form'.
Score verdict accuracy separately for the correct and incorrect halves. Pay particular attention to incorrect sentences that the model accepts, since they teach a wrong sentence as acceptable.
The level field lets you filter the eval to A1 or A2.
Run the same 42 items through each candidate model in a fresh context, then tally per-category so you can see whether failures cluster in specific categories rather than being random noise.

items.sentence: La mano derecha me duele.
items.note: mano is feminine despite ending in -o - an exception to the usual -o = masculine pattern. Correct as written.

items.sentence: El mano derecha me duele.
items.error_type: masculine article used with mano, which is a feminine exception to the -o ending pattern
items.correct_form: La mano derecha me duele.
items.note: mano ends in -o but is feminine; el mano is never correct.

items.sentence: Tengo veinticinco años.
items.note: Age is expressed with tener + años, not ser. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Soy veinticinco años.
items.error_type: ser used for age instead of tener
items.correct_form: Tengo veinticinco años.
items.note: Unlike English 'I am 25 years old', Spanish uses tener (to have) for age, not ser.

items.sentence: El hotel está muy cerca del centro.
items.note: A specific, already-identified thing's location takes estar. Correct as written.

items.sentence: El hotel hay muy cerca del centro.
items.error_type: hay used for the location of a specific/known item instead of estar
items.correct_form: El hotel está muy cerca del centro.
items.note: hay is for indefinite existence (Hay un hotel cerca); once the item is specific and known (el hotel), its location needs estar.

items.sentence: Vivo en Madrid, pero voy a Barcelona mañana.
items.note: en for location, a for direction. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Voy en Barcelona mañana.
items.error_type: en used for direction instead of a
items.correct_form: Voy a Barcelona mañana.
items.note: Movement toward a destination takes a, not en.
items.grading_context: Barcelona is the destination of the journey, not the location or means of travel.

items.sentence: Los sábados pongo la mesa y salgo con mis amigos.
items.note: poner -> pongo, salir -> salgo (irregular yo forms). Correct as written.

items.sentence: Los sábados pono la mesa y salo con mis amigos.
items.error_type: irregular first-person present forms regularized incorrectly
items.correct_form: Los sábados pongo la mesa y salgo con mis amigos.
items.note: poner and salir have irregular yo forms (pongo, salgo); 'pono'/'salo' incorrectly treat them as regular verbs.

items.sentence: Me levanto a las siete todos los días.
items.note: levantarse is used reflexively here and requires the pronoun. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Levanto a las siete todos los días.
items.error_type: missing reflexive pronoun with a reflexive verb
items.correct_form: Me levanto a las siete todos los días.
items.note: Without 'me', levanto implies lifting someone/something else, not getting oneself up.
items.grading_context: The speaker means that they get themselves out of bed at seven.

items.sentence: Sé hablar español, pero no puedo ir a la reunión hoy.
items.note: saber = learned skill; poder = situational ability/permission. Correct as written.

items.sentence: No sé ir a la reunión hoy porque trabajo.
items.error_type: saber used for situational inability where poder is required
items.correct_form: No puedo ir a la reunión hoy porque trabajo.
items.note: Being unable to attend today because of another commitment is situational, so it requires poder rather than saber.

items.sentence: Esta semana he trabajado mucho.
items.note: esta semana is an unfinished time period, so it takes perfecto (he trabajado). Correct as written.

items.sentence: Esta semana trabajé mucho.
items.error_type: indefinido used for an unfinished time period instead of perfecto
items.correct_form: Esta semana he trabajado mucho.
items.note: indefinido is for completed past periods (la semana pasada); esta semana is still ongoing, so it needs perfecto.

items.sentence: Soy médico y trabajo en el hospital central.
items.note: Profession -> ser. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Estoy médico desde hace diez años.
items.error_type: estar used for profession/identity where ser is required
items.correct_form: Soy médico desde hace diez años.
items.note: Profession is identity/definition, not a temporary state or location, so it takes ser, not estar.

items.sentence: Cuando era niño, jugaba en el parque todos los días.
items.note: Habitual past action -> imperfect. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Ayer jugaba al fútbol toda la tarde con mis amigos.
items.grading_context: The speaker intends to present this as one completed activity occupying the whole of yesterday afternoon, not as background or an activity in progress.
items.error_type: imperfect used for a single completed, bounded past event instead of preterite
items.correct_form: Ayer jugué al fútbol toda la tarde con mis amigos.
items.note: Given the stated completed-event meaning, the preterite (jugué) is required. Without that grading context, the imperfect could be valid as background or an activity in progress.

items.sentence: Compré este regalo para mi madre.
items.note: Recipient -> para. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Gracias para ayudarme con la mudanza.
items.error_type: para used where por is required for the reason for gratitude
items.correct_form: Gracias por ayudarme con la mudanza.
items.note: Gracias por introduces the action or reason for which someone is being thanked.

items.sentence: Se lo compro a Eva.
items.note: le + lo -> se lo (le/les become se before lo/la/los/las). Correct as written.

items.sentence: Le lo compro a Eva.
items.error_type: le not converted to se before a direct object pronoun
items.correct_form: Se lo compro a Eva.
items.note: Before lo/la/los/las, the indirect object pronouns le/les must change to se. 'Le lo' is never correct Spanish.

items.sentence: ¿Cuál es la tienda más cercana?
items.note: Choosing one from a known/limited set -> cuál. Correct as written.

items.sentence: ¿Qué de estas blusas quiere?
items.error_type: qué used with de to select one item from an explicit set, where cuál is required
items.correct_form: ¿Cuál de estas blusas quiere?
items.note: Cuál de selects one member of an explicit set. This avoids the regional variation around cuál used directly before a noun.

items.sentence: Ayer tuve una reunión muy larga.
items.note: tener -> irregular preterite stem tuv-. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Ayer yo hací la tarea toda la tarde.
items.error_type: irregular preterite stem regularized incorrectly
items.correct_form: Ayer yo hice la tarea toda la tarde.
items.note: hacer has the irregular preterite stem hic- (hice, hiciste, hizo...); 'hací' incorrectly treats it as a regular -er verb.

items.sentence: Me pongo triste cuando veo esa película.
items.note: ponerse + adjective = 'to become'. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Pongo triste cuando veo esa película.
items.error_type: missing reflexive pronoun changes the verb's meaning (poner vs. ponerse)
items.correct_form: Me pongo triste cuando veo esa película.
items.note: Without the reflexive pronoun, poner means 'to put/place' and needs a direct object, not an adjective describing a state - the sentence as written doesn't mean what it's trying to say.

items.sentence: Ana es muy trabajadora y dedicada.
items.note: The adjective trabajadora agrees with Ana in gender. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Ana es muy trabajador y dedicada.
items.error_type: masculine -or adjective form used with a feminine noun
items.correct_form: Ana es muy trabajadora y dedicada.
items.note: The adjective trabajador must become trabajadora to agree with Ana.

items.sentence: Aquí no se paga tanto como en otras tiendas.
items.note: Invariable tanto after a verb, comparing how much an action happens. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Aquí hay tanto ofertas como en el otro centro.
items.error_type: tanto not agreeing in gender/number with the following noun
items.correct_form: Aquí hay tantas ofertas como en el otro centro.
items.note: Before a noun, tanto must agree: tantas ofertas (feminine plural), not the invariable tanto used after a verb.

items.sentence: Ella conduce lentamente por la ciudad.
items.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective (lenta) + -mente. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Ella conduce lentomente por la ciudad.
items.error_type: masculine adjective form used instead of the feminine base before -mente
items.correct_form: Ella conduce lentamente por la ciudad.
items.note: -mente attaches to the feminine singular form of the adjective (lenta), never the masculine (lento).

items.sentence: ¡Cómpralo ahora, está muy barato!
items.note: Written accent added to preserve the original stress when a pronoun is attached to an affirmative command. Correct as written.

items.sentence: ¡Compralo ahora, está muy barato!
items.error_type: missing written accent needed to preserve stress after attaching a pronoun to an affirmative command
items.correct_form: ¡Cómpralo ahora, está muy barato!
items.note: compra + lo keeps its stress on the first syllable, which requires a written accent (cómpralo) once the pronoun is attached.

items.sentence: Vivo en Madrid desde el año 2020.
items.note: desde + starting point = 'since'. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Vivo en Madrid desde cinco años.
items.error_type: desde used with a duration instead of desde hace
items.correct_form: Vivo en Madrid desde hace cinco años.
items.note: desde needs a starting point (a date/moment); a duration continuing up to now needs desde hace + period.

items.sentence: Es un buen amigo y siempre me ayuda.
items.note: bueno shortens to buen before a masculine singular noun. Correct as written.

items.sentence: Es un bueno amigo y siempre me ayuda.
items.error_type: full form bueno used instead of the shortened buen
items.correct_form: Es un buen amigo y siempre me ayuda.
items.note: Before a masculine singular noun, bueno must shorten to buen; 'un bueno amigo' is never correct.
